Subject: Renewal planning — growth forecast & capacity ask

Hi Neha,

We’re kicking off renewal planning for our Dedicated deployment (pool ID: NC-PRD-01) and wanted to surface our growth expectations so we can lock in reserved capacity. High-level: current sustained QPS ~250 for text generation (average ~80 input+output tokens), heavy weekday traffic, and we expect peak QPS to grow ~2.5x by end of Q3 as we roll out a new chat feature.

Can Redwood recommend a renewal configuration (GPU type/count, reserved pool size, burst options) to cover a 2x–3x growth band with a 99% availability objective? Also any guidance on latency guarantees for the SLO we should ask for is helpful.

Happy to share our raw telemetry if that helps.

Thanks,

On Sun, Apr 12, 2026 at 9:18 AM Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding NovaCloud's ask. Key points: current sustained QPS ~250, avg ~80 tokens, forecasted 2–3x growth by EOY Q3, SLO target ~99% availability.

Attached a quick model (capacity-modeling-v2.xlsx) — summary below. Assumptions: average seq len 80 tokens, decode 1 token/step, model variant used: redwood-chat-large quantized. Batch arrival distribution: median 8 reqs, p95 batch size 28. KV cache hit assumed 25% initially (they said heavy weekday traffic).

Conservative renewal (cost-optimized):
- Reserved pool: 4 x H100-equivalent GPUs (steady-state capacity)
- Autoscale burst: +2 GPUs available for spikes (on-demand for 30% of spike traffic)
- Rationale: at 2x sustained (500 QPS) model, 4 H100s with batch tuning and cache hit ~25% covers ~85% of traffic within p95 < 300ms; 2 GPU burst handles p99 spikes.

Aggressive renewal (performance-guaranteed):
- Reserved pool: 6 x H100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated)
- Guaranteed throughput: capacity to support 650–750 QPS sustained with p95 latency target < 250ms (with current batching)
- Canaries & rollout: reserve 1 GPU (10–15%) for canary traffic during major rollouts, recommend 14-day canary before full cutover.

Notes/alternatives:
- Mixed fleet: 4 x H100 + 2 x A100 (cheaper) if they accept slightly higher p95 for some tail workloads.
- If NovaCloud increases cache hit to 45% (via prefix caching) we can drop 1 GPU from each config.

I attached the modeling sheet with token/sec throughput per GPU, queueing assumptions, and cost delta estimates (on an annual reserved contract). Let me know if you want me to surface a pricing delta for both.

—Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal planning — growth forecast & capacity ask

Marissa — good modeling. A few operational caveats to add to the customer-facing recommendation: 
- Measured throughput (redwood-chat-large quantized): ~28–32 requests/s per H100 at avg 80 tokens with batch size 24–32 (depends on request length distribution).
- For steady 500–650 qps: recommend batch_size target=32, max latency guardrails (soft) at 350ms; p95s tighten to ~220–260ms in our sims with KV cache 20–30%.
- Autoscale policy: steady reserved pool + a burst pool of 2 GPUs (pre-warmed) with scaling threshold at 70% CPU/GPU util. Add a 10% headroom margin for noisy neighbors and model warmup.
- Canary strategy: route 10% of traffic to new pool for 48–72 hours, compare token-level quality and latency; rollback fast path in 15 minutes.

Operational ask for NovaCloud: provide a 7–day high-resolution trace (1s granularity) if possible so we can tune the batch window more precisely. I’ll add the HubSpot link to the renewal proposal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/7392).

—Rishi

- Operational config: batch_size target 32, KV cache enabled, 10% canary for rollouts, 48–72 hour canary window
- Throughput/latency commitments: capacity to sustain 650 QPS with p95 latency target < 250ms under modeled token distribution; on-call escalation SLA per enterprise T&C

Cost note: attaching a short pricing draft (renewal-pricing-draft.pdf) that shows annual reserved pricing vs. mixed-fleet alternative (4 H100 + 2 A100). If NovaCloud prefers the cost-optimized option we can price that separately.
